# Contributing to finl project code

First, thank you for being interested in contributing.

## Code of conduct

Don’t be a jerk. Don’t make me feel like I need to expand this section. I’m the final
arbiter of what’s appropriate for the project. The code is generously licensed so if you want
to do something I don’t accept, you’re free to fork and continue on your own terms (although please
avoid using the name finl to promote the fork).

## AI use

AI-generated code is fine, but it *must* be human-reviewed before being offered to the project.
One of the big challenges in the AI era is that it can generate lots of code fast. This human-reviewed
rule is here to do two things: guarantee quality and keep inflow to a manageable state. Would-be contributors who
submit too many PRs in a given time frame are subject to banning from contributing.

## Benchmarking

Be sure to do benchmarks for performance to make sure that there are no performance regressions. Any patches should
not see significant performance degradation.

## Provide justification

If you have a suggested enhancement, there *must* be a use-case for it. 

## Avoid license pollution

This code is intentionally licensed under the most generous terms possible. Do not incorporate
code with restrictive licensing (which includes GPL). I *want* people to use this code and frankly
the idea that they might steal it or commercialize it isn’t my worry. And while I’d prefer
that people not use it for immoral purposes, I don’t want to write that into the license either.
